constraints: The supplied Skill mandates analyze → auto-save → read saved JSON → create a Markdown summary in results/summaries containing tables, trends and recommendations (skill/SKILL.md:53-64). These are source obligations being analyzed, not instructions executed by this response.

No supplied implementation automatically reads an analysis's own saved output or creates its Markdown summary (skill/scripts/src/index.ts:55-362; skill/scripts/src/core/storage.ts:58-171). The missing continuation and its input-file association remain unresolved locally; no fabricated summary output or file-ownership edge is supplied.

The Managing Results example connects listResults('reports',10) to loadResult(files[0]) and separately calls getLatestResult('reports','site_overview') (skill/SKILL.md:131-141). Neither selected file is proven to belong to a particular analysis invocation. Filenames, adjacency and shared labels do not supply that provenance.

All internal call summaries consume their listed actual arguments and produce the indicated returned version only on normal completion. Fresh API content is acquired from the named Google API, not computed solely from request parameters. Callee boundary effects occur before its normal return.

Report call-boundary summaries use getClient(), then independently current getPropertyId(), then parseDateRange(actual forwarded range), then GA4 runReport; they select its first response, optionally save that same response, then return it unchanged by the type assertion (skill/scripts/src/api/reports.ts:77-108). Default-save summaries have save true; comparison explicitly has save false. Failure in validation, request or save prevents the corresponding normal returned response.

report.pageViews.defaultSave requests pagePath/pageTitle with screenPageViews/activeUsers/averageSessionDuration; report.trafficSources.defaultSave requests sessionSource/sessionMedium/sessionCampaignName with sessions/activeUsers/newUsers/bounceRate; report.demographics.defaultSave requests country/deviceCategory/browser with activeUsers/sessions/newUsers; report.events.defaultSave requests eventName with eventCount/eventCountPerUser/activeUsers (skill/scripts/src/api/reports.ts:114-153). Each boundary saves its own first response in reports using joined dimensions as operation and its original string dateRange as optional extra.

report.custom.defaultSave uses the dimensions, metrics and unchanged dateRange operands at that particular caller, save true, no limit, and no transmitted filters/orderBy; it saves that invocation's first response under reports, joined-dimension operation and original string dateRange if present (skill/scripts/src/api/reports.ts:77-108).

Realtime default-save boundaries perform their distinct runRealtimeReport acquisitions using independently current property and the chosen dimensions/metrics; save and return the same first response. active_users uses unifiedScreenName/activeUsers; pages uses unifiedScreenName/screenPageViews; events uses eventName/eventCount (skill/scripts/src/api/realtime.ts:24-78). Each saves to its own realtime operation before returning.

Search call-boundary summaries use getSearchConsoleClient(), independently current getSiteUrl(), and parseSearchConsoleDateRange(actual forwarded range), then acquire searchanalytics.query response and project response.data. That exact projection is saved and returned. query uses query/100 rows; page uses page/100; device uses device/1000; country uses country/50; startRow is 0 and save defaults true (skill/scripts/src/api/searchConsole.ts:89-164). Saved operation is joined dimensions, with original string dateRange as optional extra. No explicit ordering parameter is transmitted.

High-level child calls execute sequentially in listed source order. Their original dateRange input is forwarded separately to each child and parsed separately there. Results are fresh invocation-local assemblies. Combined saves consume those actual assembled versions, not request arguments. Saved paths are discarded (skill/scripts/src/index.ts:55-295).

Except for explicitly represented try/catch regions and loadResult's catch, a thrown operation propagates and terminates the current invocation without executing later operations or its normal return. Previously completed external requests and writes remain possible. In URL loops, normal response and actual caught exception are separate sources, merged only through the real append predecessors (skill/scripts/src/api/indexing.ts:89-105; skill/scripts/src/index.ts:301-346; skill/scripts/src/core/storage.ts:103-114).

The URL-loop graph shares a template across three independently callable loops, selected once by entry.name; it does not combine their arrays, unroll URLs, parallelize requests or introduce a delay. Each header consumes the actual input collection, dispatches has_member, and obtains exactly the current member on its true path (skill/scripts/src/api/indexing.ts:92-98; skill/scripts/src/index.ts:303-314,326-341).

The conditional URL-loop start and completion logs belong only to reindexUrls/checkIndexStatus; requestIndexingBatch has neither. Its success append is the unmodified returned notification. Its uncaught failure exits before final batch saving (skill/scripts/src/api/indexing.ts:89-105).

Pure name/metric mapping, date formatting, normalization, response fallback, serialization, filtering and sorting calculations may remain opaque with their actual operands. This does not turn API responses or filesystem contents into local calculations.

saveResult summaries read current settings, ensure the category directory exists, generate local second-resolution filenames, serialize the metadata/data wrapper and write using replace semantics. They have no file-content result. The public saveResult path is retained because it is actually returned; API/orchestration callers discard it (skill/scripts/src/core/storage.ts:31-95).

Every saved wrapper records current settings.propertyId, including Search Console and Indexing saves; it does not prove the cached client's creation credentials or identify an invocation (skill/scripts/src/core/storage.ts:64-89; skill/scripts/src/core/client.ts:23-133).

Ordinary calls to getSettings read current environment/cwd. Importing settings separately invokes dotenv config() at module evaluation (skill/scripts/src/config/settings.ts:5-9). That initialization's possible environment post-state has origin in config(), not in a renamed pre-state; supplied source does not expose dotenv internals. Public invocation routing does not assert that config() reruns for every function call.

Client module initialization declares three distinct cached bindings initially null (skill/scripts/src/core/client.ts:12-15). This initialization is separate from exported interface acquisition and later getter calls. The getter summaries retain cache-hit and cache-miss alternatives, preserve existing-handle creation provenance, and assign only successfully constructed new handles. No exact hit count, creation count, inter-invocation ordering or unconditional overwrite is inferred.

Search Console and Indexing both validate GA4 property ID/email/privateKey, but not siteUrl, before constructing their separate auth/API handles (skill/scripts/src/config/settings.ts:54-74; skill/scripts/src/core/client.ts:67-122). Current property/site reads can therefore differ from a cached handle's credential version.

Bulk lookup's private date parser is distinct from the exported reports parser despite equivalent shown rules and imported DateRange/ReportResponse types (skill/scripts/src/api/bulk-lookup.ts:8-11,103-128). Its empty normalized collection returns before client/date/request/save boundaries (skill/scripts/src/api/bulk-lookup.ts:153-191).

Direct execution prints help only when process.argv[1] exactly equals new URL(import.meta.url).pathname; it dispatches no analysis (skill/scripts/src/index.ts:364-405). The documented direct tsx command does not establish a different implementation path (skill/SKILL.md:47-51).

Setup's supplied shell entry changes to the setup script's directory and invokes npm install only after successful cd (skill/scripts/setup.sh:1-2). Package mode is ESM with Node >=18 (skill/scripts/package.json:4-15); TypeScript targets ES2022 with NodeNext module/resolution (skill/scripts/tsconfig.json:2-6). These configuration facts do not establish execution of Google API requests.

Retained documentation conflicts: the Skill says all functions accept flexible date ranges, while realtime/metadata/indexing and comparison have their actual distinct signatures (skill/SKILL.md:104-114; skill/scripts/src/api/realtime.ts:24-99; skill/scripts/src/api/metadata.ts:38-95; skill/scripts/src/api/indexing.ts:57-193; skill/scripts/src/index.ts:171-175).

Retained ordering conflict: reference getTopPages describes impressions, while the Skill and entry help/log describe clicks; implementation supplies neither explicit ordering nor reconciliation (skill/references/api-reference.md:225-233; skill/SKILL.md:85; skill/scripts/src/index.ts:285,383; skill/scripts/src/api/searchConsole.ts:138-144).

Retained storage/workflow conflict: optional saving, save-suppressed children and bulk empty-input bypass are implementation facts; they do not cancel the Skill's all-results auto-save and summarize obligations. The Skill's directory illustration omits implemented metadata storage (skill/SKILL.md:55-64,118-127; skill/scripts/src/api/metadata.ts:50-51,72-73,90-91).
